The Age of Fighting Sail
The words, in plain English
Rake: fire into her bow or stern, down the length of her decks.
Broadside: all the guns on one side, fired together.
Strike her colours: surrender. She stops firing but is not yours yet.
Prize: a captured ship. She flies your flag and does not fight.
Close-hauled: as near the wind as she will lie.
No-go zone: the wedge she cannot sail into. Shaded on the chart.
In irons: stuck head to wind, no way on, helm dead.
Steerage way: the speed the rudder needs to bite, about 1.5 knots.
Spring: a rope that swings an anchored ship so her guns bear.
Weather gage: being upwind. You choose when to close.
Rate: her size by gun count. First is biggest, sixth a frigate.
Ship of the line: big enough to fight in the line: third rate or better.
Pistol shot: about 50 m. Damage rises steeply inside 120 m.
Wear: turn by putting her stern through the wind.
Wind sets your speed. The shaded wedge is forbidden. Fastest with the wind on your beam.
A rake fires down her whole length. Twice damage across her bow, three times across her stern.
Round hulls, any range. Chain masts, under 400 m. Grape crew, under 300 m. Double hulls, under 250 m. A chooses for you.
Board only a beaten ship. A fresh crew throws you back. Grape her decks first. The bar is your party against hers.
At anchor you shoot straighter but cannot move. A spring swings her to keep guns bearing. Forts never surrender.
Yours gold, enemy blue, struck bone white. Bar is hull, dots are crew, masts are rig. A word beneath says why she cannot move.
